title: Two Turns on Repeat
statement: A robot stands at a point $O$ on a flat floor, facing north. It carries out the following four instructions in this order, and then repeats them again and again: move forward $1$ metre; turn $100^\circ$ clockwise; move forward $1$ metre; turn $140^\circ$ clockwise. After how many moves forward does the robot first finish a move at $O$?
hints: Group the moves in pairs: one pair is a move, the $100^\circ$ turn, a move and the $140^\circ$ turn. Compare each pair of moves with the pair before it.

Each pair turns the robot through $100^\circ + 140^\circ = 240^\circ$ clockwise, which is $120^\circ$ anticlockwise. So the displacement of each pair is the displacement of the previous pair rotated by $120^\circ$, and three such displacements form an equilateral triangle.

After a whole number of pairs, the robot's position is the sum of the pair displacements. To check that no earlier move ends at $O$, find the distance from $O$ after $2$ and after $4$ moves, and compare it with $0$ and with $1$ metre, the length of the next move.
solution:
Let $v$ be the displacement made by the first two moves. Each pair of moves turns the robot $240^\circ$ clockwise, that is $120^\circ$ anticlockwise, so the next pairs make $v$ rotated by $120^\circ$ and by $240^\circ$. These three vectors sum to zero, so the robot is at $O$ after $6$ moves.

The two moves of $v$ meet at an angle of $180^\circ - 100^\circ = 80^\circ$, so $|v| = 2\sin 40^\circ$, which is neither $0$ nor $1$. After $2$ or $4$ moves the robot is at distance $|v|$ from $O$, as $v$ plus $v$ rotated by $120^\circ$ has the same length as $v$. After $1$, $3$ or $5$ moves it is $1$ metre from where it was after $0$, $2$ or $4$ moves, and that point is $O$ itself or at distance $|v| \ne 1$ from $O$. So it is not at $O$ before move $6$, and the answer is $6$.

solution_figures.alt: The robot's path from O: six moves of 1 metre, starting north, with turns of 100 and 140 degrees clockwise in turn. P1 to P5 are its positions after 1 to 5 moves, and the sixth move ends at O. The moves meet at P1 at an angle of 80 degrees. The points O, P2 and P4, reached after 0, 2 and 4 moves, form an equilateral triangle with side 2 sin 40 degrees, drawn dashed with its sides highlighted, because each pair of moves is the previous pair rotated by 120 degrees.
